OurFineSplatrepresents scenes more accurately and preserves the fine details while using the same or smaller Gaussian budgets.

Figure 2:Method Overview.FineSplatfirst performs view-wise grouping and applies self-attention within each group, enabling efficient processing of fine-grained tokens. 3D spatial grouping lifts tokens into 3D space and enables interactions among spatially neighboring tokens, including those from different view groups, to enhance cross-view information exchange. Compact Gaussian generation predicts fewer Gaussians per token than existing pixel-aligned methods, maintaining a compact 3DGS representation. Finally, direct error feedback incorporates reconstruction errors obtained by rendering the input views to further refine token representations.

Figure 9:Comparison of resizing filters.From left to right, an original high-resolution image and its downsampled versions using PIL Lanczos and bilinear interpolation with anti-aliasing (Bilinear+AA).
Lanczos better preserves high-frequency details such as the thin cracks and surface texture, whereas Bilinear+AA produces a smoother image in which these details are partly lost.
